clue.text: The time of life when one ages, figuratively speaking

definitions.text: The time of life when one ages, figuratively speaking

parts.words: The time of life when one ages, figuratively speaking
parts.note: read figuratively, 'ages' means grows a year older, which happens on one particular anniversary each year

explanation.definitionFit: The anniversary of one's birth is the day on which one's age goes up by a year.

clue.text: Fashionable —- opposite of passive or lethargic

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
active is the opposite of passive

explanation.surface: A list of contrasts: trendy, energetic or sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means not moving or doing anything, the state of someone sluggish.

clue.text: Strain over first of exams essay done without cheating

indicators.note: done without says the attempt's word goes outside the other pieces

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try

indicators.note: over says the strain comes above the next letter in this down entry

parts.note: a rick is a sprain or strain

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the word exams

explanation.surface: A student under exam strain writes an essay honestly, without cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickery is deception or cheating.

clue.text: Quickly avoided noise in the Tube

indicators.note: noise says the word for quickly avoided is said aloud

parts.note: to duck is to dodge quickly, so ducked

explanation.surface: Someone dodges a din on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is just any tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a tube or channel carrying fluid or air.

clue.text: Dog's noise has given one gyp — pain, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dog's barking has given someone gyp, a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yapping is the shrill barking of a small dog.

clue.text: Found union membership that's expedient

parts.note: found a union reads as joining a trade union, but here the union is a wedding arranged for convenience

explanation.definitionFit: To marry off a child is to find them a husband or wife, often as a convenient arrangement.

clue.text: Intend boy's upbringing to include studying in part of SE Europe

indicators.note: to include says the studying word goes inside
upbringing in a down clue means the words are read upwards

parts.note: to aim is to intend
a lad is a boy
at means studying, as at university

explanation.surface: A parent wants their son's education to include study abroad in the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' works because this is a down entry: the reversed words are read bottom to top, giving DALMIA before the studying word goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is a coastal region of Croatia on the Adriatic, in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Given no guidance in choice of petrol

definitions.meaning: freed from a lead, nobody leading
unleaded fuel, sold as a grade of petrol

explanation.definitionFit: Lead-free petrol contains no lead; read as lead free, it means without leadership.

clue.text: Mother, among a lot of special offers, found type of water

indicators.note: among says the mother's word sits in the middle of the special-offers phrase

parts.note: a sale is a lot of special offers, giving A SALE
a dam is a mother animal, as in horse breeding

explanation.surface: A mother finds a brand of bottled water while browsing the bargains.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain drinking water, Adam having had nothing else to drink.

clue.text: Sets competition record, holding a 21 up

indicators.note: holding means the record's word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
21 across is FIVE, which as a Roman numeral is V
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis competitor's record holds up well at the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer of 21 across, a number, given here as its Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davis Cup is the international men's team tennis competition, and tennis matches are played in sets.

clue.text: Fed English rump, cooked with tempting aroma

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A cut of beef is cooked so that it smells delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfumed is scented, giving off a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Sort of Green caught in dodgy club, being different

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside the club's word

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable nightclub or bar

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters of the word green are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Some kind of environmentalist is found in a seedy nightclub, standing out from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour or an environmentalist; 'Sort of' rearranges it, and a dive is a seedy club.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergence is the state of departing from a norm, i.e. being different.

clue.text: Wanting to get a round in here, before driving off?

definitions.text: Wanting to get a round in here, before driving off?

parts.words: Wanting to get a round in here, before driving off?
parts.note: reads as buying drinks in a pub before driving, but the round is eighteen holes and driving off is the first tee shot

explanation.definitionFit: A course for golf is where a round is played, starting with the tee shot or drive.

clue.text: Can sentence cause trouble?

definitions.meaning: time in the can, slang for prison; slang for jail
to ... is to ... up trouble or agitate

explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison and also means to make mischief between people.

clue.text: Muster resources, being down in the dumps

definitions.text: Muster resources, being down in the dumps

parts.words: Muster resources, being down in the dumps
parts.note: the dumps here are rubbish tips, where materials are gathered up to be used again, not a low mood

explanation.definitionFit: To process waste so it can be reused is to make new resources from what was discarded.

clue.text: Smart fan set out to see someone plying their craft

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A smart supporter goes out to watch an expert at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' is a boat or raft here, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A raftsman is someone who steers a raft, a kind of water craft.

clue.text: One almost furious being held up by vessel, non-military

indicators.note: held says the pieces sit inside the vessel's word

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel

indicators.note: up in a down clue means those letters read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the furious word is dropped

parts.note: livid means furious

explanation.surface: Someone almost livid is held up by a ship's crew, a non-combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' does two things in a down entry: 'up' turns the one-plus-almost-furious letters upwards, and 'held' puts them inside the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian is a person not in the armed forces.

clue.text: Bouquet of claret, originally, or added herb?

indicators.note: added says the herb comes on at the end
originally points to the opening letter of the word claret

parts.note: taken as written
sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A wine taster describes the nose of a claret, wondering if a herb has been added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' pretends to be the wine's aroma; it is a small bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small bouquet of flowers worn on a dress.

clue.text: Male celebrity initially sounds confused in racing vehicle

indicators.note: the opening sounds of the two words are muddled, swapping places

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A male star gets his words mixed up in a racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening C of COCK and ST of STAR gives STOCK CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is a modified saloon car raced on oval tracks.

clue.text: May king hang about to see this riding event?

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A May king hangs about to watch a riding competition.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymkhana is a local horse-riding competition, common for children in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is an event of riding races and contests for horses and riders.

clue.text: The opposite of how poetry is written -

definitions.meaning: the reverse or contrary of something

explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means opposite, and split it describes poetry being written in verse.

clue.text: A number of famous young heroes

definitions.meaning: a number such as four or six
Enid Blyton's Famous ..., a gang of child adventurers in British children's books

explanation.definitionFit: It is a number and the count in Enid Blyton's Famous Five, the children's adventure series.

clue.text: Complex problem involving amateur angler's bait?

definitions.meaning: an issue that, once opened, causes many more difficulties
taken literally, a tin of worms used as fishing bait

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a situation full of unforeseen complications; literally it is a tin of bait.

clue.text: Avoiding company cutting reliable duet for performance

indicators.note: cutting means trimming the last letter off the reliable word

parts.note: solid means dependable or reliable

indicators.note: for performance suggests the word duet is reworked, as if staged

explanation.surface: A loner gives up a dependable duet act to perform alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' trims SOLID to SOLI; 'for performance' rearranges DUET into TUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitude is the state of being alone, keeping away from other people.

clue.text: -- one's been taken up on it!

definitions.text: one's been taken up on it!

parts.words: one's been taken up on it!
parts.note: being taken up suggests lifted to a height, but also the euphoric state after taking drugs

explanation.definitionFit: Being on a high means elated or intoxicated, raised up as if lifted.

clue.text: Protection from falling income in prevailing climate?

definitions.text: Protection from falling income in prevailing climate?

parts.words: Protection from falling income in prevailing climate?
parts.note: sounds like insurance in a recession, but what falls is water from the sky in a wet climate

explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat is protection from rain falling from the sky.

clue.text: An intro to Aristophanes' Lysistrata, half written, in study

indicators.note: intro to points to the opening letter of the playwright's name
half signals taking the first half of the play's title

explanation.surface: A classics student begins the Greek comic play, half finishing a written study.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of LYSISTRATA (10 letters) is LYSIS. 'written' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a detailed study or examination of something.

clue.text: At last, the genuine article's included — it's heavenly

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word the

parts.note: the is the definite article
real means genuine

explanation.surface: Finally the real thing turns up, and it is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' says the article is put into the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and light as if of the heavens, so it is heavenly.
